A.basis: state-machine-as-value is the row's lowest form; every other cell is it plus a bundled runtime choice (event loop = executor atop polled futures; Java's hidden suspension = a scheduler service decision)

B.basis: virtues don't co-occur: Go has ergonomics + select; Dart has the isolation guarantee; Rust has the transfer proof (Send). No language holds all three
B.in_hub: three-virtue composite: Go's ergonomics (channel/spawn/select spellings, scheduler polyfill) + Dart's isolation guarantee (dev-time border check: no mutable object crosses spawn) + Rust's transfer proof (send checked at dev-time, a Ledger judgment)

C.basis: Option<T> with no null in the language; every other cell is it weakened (sugar removed, enforcement removed, or null retained alongside)

D.basis: exhaustive + deep destructuring subsumes the row; C#'s pattern richness reduces to guards

E.basis: structural (Go/TS) and nominal (Java/Kotlin) conformance are different intentions; no language offers both first-class. The row origin qualifiers exist for
E.in_hub: dual conformance regimes, qualifier-selected (go.interface structural, java.interface nominal); run-time residue identical (map from type to function); structural-into-nominal requires explicit `as` spelling

F.basis: reified subsumes erased; C++ template computation reassigned to row J, leaving pure parameterization, which C# covers
F.in_hub: restricted below C#: dev-time parameterization only, no run-time type queries (reification is a permission and egresses hard)

G.basis: Drop is automatic; every explicit spelling (with, using, defer, ensure) is a drop-guard value; Go's function-exit variant reproducible

H.basis: streams subsume callbacks/delegates/multicast; best native versions in C#/Dart, but the true satisfier is the derived object (collection of function-values + suspension)
H.in_hub: streams as the canonical superset, built as the derived object (collection of function-values + suspension); born as a polyfill, egress is its definition

I.basis: Swift: new symbols + precedence, everything else a subset. Rust: overloading-as-trait, the cleanest mechanism for a merged language
I.in_hub: trait-based operator overloading (Rust mechanism); novel symbols (Swift) at-own-risk

J.basis: the row spans three stages (run-time mutation, dev-time transforms, type-level); table 2's conflicts show run-time mutation destroys the proofs everything else depends on. The row must be truncated (dev-time only), not satisfied
J.in_hub: the row is truncated, not satisfied: J1 dev-time codegen unrestricted; J2 run-time read as closed-world reflection over the Ledger (egress emits metadata tables); J3 run-time write gated by the egress-coverage analyzer (narrow target set + voided proofs, knowingly accepted)

A.C#: origin of async/await; Task as first-class handle; the reference state-machine transform
A.C++: C++20 coroutines: rawest form — transform exposed as customization points; no standard runtime
A.Dart: async/await + async* generators; one event loop per isolate; compiler state-machine
A.Go: — (goroutines subsume the intent; see channels row)
A.Java: — as syntax; virtual threads instead: make blocking cheap, hide suspension rather than spell it
A.Kotlin: suspend functions; compiler state-machine; adds structured concurrency scopes
A.PHP: Fibers since 8.1; no async syntax; rare under request-per-process model
A.Python: async/await + generators; cooperative event loop (asyncio); interpreted, not compiled transform
A.Ruby: Fibers: explicit resume, no async syntax; scheduler hook since 3.0
A.Rust: async fn compiles to a state-machine VALUE (Future); inert until polled; runtime is a library choice
A.Swift: async/await + actors; structured concurrency like Kotlin
A.TypeScript: async/await lowered to promises/generators; single-threaded event loop

B.Dart: isolates + ports: messaging is the ONLY concurrency; purest actor stance
B.Go: channels + goroutines are the language identity; select is syntax-level
B.Java: BlockingQueue library; virtual threads make thread-per-message viable
B.Python: library queues (queue, asyncio, multiprocessing); GIL limits parallelism
B.Rust: std mpsc; unique: Send trait — transfer safety proven at compile-time
B.TypeScript: postMessage between workers; structured clone — no shared objects

C.C#: nullable reference types, opt-in annotations; Nullable<T> for values
C.C++: std::optional for values only; raw pointers still null
C.Dart: sound null safety in the type system (T?)
C.Go: nil + (value, ok) multiple-return idiom; no type-level option
C.Java: Optional<T> as a library object; null remains everywhere else
C.Kotlin: T? enforced in the type system
C.Rust: Option<T> pure sum type; no null exists at all — strongest form
C.Swift: Optional IS an enum — sum type with ? ! sugar
C.TypeScript: union types T | null | undefined; strictNullChecks flag

D.Java: switch patterns + record deconstruction; sealed exhaustive
D.Kotlin: when + smart casts; sealed exhaustiveness; shallow destructuring
D.Rust: match is central: exhaustive, deep destructuring — reference realization
D.TypeScript: — native; discriminated unions + narrowing carry the intent

E.C#: nominal + default impls; explicit implementation option
E.C++: — as such; virtual classes or templates; concepts (C++20) are structural constraints
E.Dart: every class IS an implicit interface — unique
E.Go: structural interfaces, implicit satisfaction — no conformance declaration
E.Python: duck typing; Protocols structural but unenforced; ABCs
E.Rust: traits with coherence (orphan rule); monomorphized by default, dyn opt-in
E.Swift: protocols + extensions + associated types; protocol-oriented identity
E.TypeScript: structural everywhere — interfaces are shapes, not contracts

F.C#: reified in the CLR — run-time knows T
F.C++: templates — monomorphization origin; compile-time duck typing until concepts
F.Go: type parameters (1.18), constraint interfaces; deliberately minimal
F.Rust: monomorphization: compile-time copy per type; zero-cost
F.TypeScript: fully erased; types vanish at run-time

G.Go: defer — fires at FUNCTION exit, not scope exit (unique gotcha)
G.Rust: Drop trait: automatic, ownership-driven — no spelling at use site

H.C#: delegates + event ARE language constructs; multicast — unique
H.C++: lambdas with explicit capture lists — capture spelled manually
H.Go: function values; channels often replace callbacks
H.Java: functional interfaces + SAM conversion — function-as-value encoded as interface
H.Ruby: blocks/procs/lambdas — three callable kinds; implicit block argument unique
H.Rust: closures with TYPED capture modes (move) — capture is part of the type

I.C++: origin; all existing operators, no new symbols
I.Rust: trait-based (Add, Mul): overloading IS trait implementation
I.Swift: can define NEW operator symbols + precedence — most permissive

J.C#: reflection + source generators + expression trees (code as data) — unique
J.C++: templates: accidentally Turing-complete dev-time metaprogramming; constexpr; no reflection
J.Dart: — run-time (mirrors dead in Flutter); dev-time codegen instead
J.PHP: run-time reflection API + attributes + magic methods
J.Python: maximal run-time: metaclasses, __getattr__, decorators, full introspection
J.Ruby: maximal: method_missing, define_method, open classes — the language's identity
J.Rust: no run-time reflection; macros — powerful dev-time syntax transforms
J.TypeScript: metaprograms in the TYPE system (mapped/conditional types), erased — unique
